items.note: gram_compression states the lemma under the hypotheses of Theorem art:minor-hierarchy (energy.tex:130-141), written out: H ≻ 0, s = -αHg, α > 0, q = gᵀHg > 0, β = -yᵀHg/q > 0, H₊ = inverseBFGS H s y (the update art:update), for Z : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin j) ℝ with Zᵀ * Z = 1 and 1 ≤ j ≤ n. Its conclusion is the inequality of disp/001 and, for the last sentence, j = n → det H₊ = (α/β) det H. Gram_H(y,Z) = [y Z]ᵀH[y Z] (defined at energy.tex:150) is metricGram H (fromCols (replicateCol Unit y) Z). The proof follows the paper, from the display theorems of this module. det_update states det H₊ = (α/β) det H without Z (second proof, from the library's inverseBFGS_step_det_beta). The library's compressed_inverseBFGS_bound is the inequality for every Z with independent columns.

gram_compression is proved along this proof. Besides the displays (own items), the module states the undisplayed steps: kappa_eq_and_curvature (lines 14-15: κ = gᵀHy = -βq, yᵀs = αβq), gram_dets_nonneg (49-50), compression_update and compression_add_rank_one (58-62: ZᵀH₊Z = Zᵀ𝓕Z + ρaaᵀ with ρ = α/(βq); adding ρaaᵀ replaces r/κ² by r/κ² + ρ and adds exactly ρ det A u to the determinant), u_bounds (62-64: det Gram_H(g,Z) = (q-u) det A, 0 ≤ u ≤ q, increase ≤ (α/β) det A), full_dimension_case (67-71: for j = n, ZZᵀ = I, u = q, w = κ, z = r, det(Zᵀ𝓕Z) = 0, increase = (α/β) det A, det(ZᵀH₊Z) = (α/β) det A, det H₊ = (α/β) det H). All hold as written. Corrected on 15 October 2026 (M34, M38, M39): the two wording points noted here are resolved: Gram_H(g,Z) = [g Z]ᵀH[g Z] and Gram_H(g,y,Z) = [g y Z]ᵀH[g y Z] are defined before the display (lines 41-42; Gram_H(y,Z) is energy.tex:150), the Schur complement is credited only with u ≤ q ("and u ≥ 0 since A ≻ 0", line 63); also the scalar factors are written first ((r - z) det A), the value ρ = α/(βq) is tied to the compression through Zᵀv = a (lines 61-62), Z is "an orthogonal matrix, A⁻¹ = ZᵀH⁻¹Z" for j = n and the right side of (art:compression-determinant) vanishes (lines 67-69); end-of-proof mark.
Stated with v, κ, P, 𝓕 (Lean F) as variables with their defining equations v = Hg, κ = gᵀHy, P = I - vyᵀ/κ, F = PHPᵀ.

The display defines A, a, b, r, u, w, z and asserts A = ZᵀHZ ≻ 0. compression_posDef states the assertion. The definitions are notation: the coverage theorems of disp/004 to disp/006 take the ones they use as variables with exactly these defining equations as hypotheses (e.g. hu : u = dot a (A⁻¹ *ᵥ a)).
[a b] is (Matrix.of ![a, b])ᵀ, so [a b]ᵀ is Matrix.of ![a, b].
